# Transparent SVG over an external backdrop

Original control generated by tools/svg_external_backdrop_fixture.py; no corpus
artwork or fonts. Nine rows contain four colors at 0.1/0.3 opacity and one
pair of overlapping fills. There is no opaque SVG background. The existing
original picture generator places it as a picture, crop, group and shape fill.

The reference application opened the source read-only. Range.EnhMetaFileBits supplies the
first picture's native nested metafile. Windows GDI+ draws that metafile over
four opaque bitmap backgrounds. native-colors.json binds source, cases, native
captures and four reference bitmaps by SHA-256. These are native-metafile
references, not a claim to have sampled the reference application's window or PDF raster colors.

Regeneration (reference application required):

1. Run python tools/svg_external_backdrop_fixture.py.
2. Run tools/capture-svg-backdrop-metafile.ps1 with -Python pointing to Python
   and -FixtureDirectory tests/fixtures/svg-external-backdrop.
3. Run tools/record-svg-external-backdrop.ps1.
4. Run tests/svg-external-backdrop.test.js and the corresponding browser spec.

The browser test is deliberately an expected failure. On Edge, 28 of 36 flat
samples agree; four low-opacity samples over #202020 and all four overlaps
fail. On #F2F2F2, overlapping fills are native (238,221,204) versus browser
(237,221,203). The plain teal sample agrees with the native reference even
though PDFium's rendering of the corpus PDF differs by one channel. Therefore
changing the source color to match the PDF alone would not be justified.

This closes an evidence gap in the internal-backdrop control: the discrepancy
also exists when the backdrop is outside the SVG. Correcting only fills over
an internal opaque rectangle cannot fix transparent pictures over document
content. Layer order, target backdrop, alpha rounding and edge coverage must
remain distinguishable; a single flattened RGBA image is not assumed to prove
equivalence to native per-layer blending. Clipping, gradients, transforms and
partially covered pixels need coverage before a general correction is shipped.

No renderer behavior changes in this commit. This is a regression oracle,
not a passing rendering test or a claim of a specification divergence. Source
over is specified mathematically; these finite-precision differences require
native implementation evidence. The existing ECMA-376 picture/extension
references and SVG compositing rules apply.

Validation: two provenance unit tests pass (this and the internal-backdrop
control). The expected-failure browser test reproduces all eight recorded
mismatches. The control is editable with no runtime errors, exact no-edit ZIP,
body edit with unrelated parts preserved, exact undo and reopening. Its source
passes ten XML checks; three exports pass thirty more. The concurrently
rechecked corpus #57 exports pass 39 checks. No runtime/dependency changes.

A 2026-10-10 diagnostic
also checks the retained alpha-only candidate and ten separate SVG paint images
over each of these four backgrounds. All three browser paths retain 28/36 exact
center matches; separating image draws does not resolve the native discrepancy.
Separate byte rounding matches the 36 native centers numerically, with edge
coverage and a general production correction still open.
